blocks.text: Job 27 belongs to the sustained debate that follows seven days of shared silence. Job’s friends increasingly explain his suffering as the result of wrongdoing, while Job rejects that diagnosis. This context helps explain why he so firmly refuses to surrender his integrity in this chapter.

A later interpretation connects Job with endurance and the compassionate outcome of his story. Here, however, Job’s steadfastness is not silent compliance: he continues to speak, protest, and maintain his integrity. This interpretation should not be used to require silent endurance of abuse or to discourage escape and protection.
